what_it_is: The card opens as a fake system starting up. Typed terminal lines roast one real trait, then 'Press any key' unlocks the card. The tap doubles as the browser's permission to play sound.

A hero line that always knows what day it is. Before the birthday it counts down, on the day it celebrates, and after it turns lateness into a joke and shows how long until the next one. One link works whenever it is opened.
best_for: Anyone; especially late cards and children's countdowns
lineage: Jordan.EXE: birthday opening and date logic (C-HERO)

what_it_is: The recipient's name as a stylized logo built from their own world: cut-out ransom-note letters, chain and gears, coffee stains, neon, pixel blocks, chalk. It opens the card and becomes the share preview.
A silver panel the recipient scratches with a finger to reveal a message: the big age, a plan, a gift. Small decoy spots pay off with tiny gags before the main reveal.
best_for: Kids, milestone birthdays, any surprise reveal

what_it_is: A 20-second text trailer of big title cards: 'In a world where...', real details as plot points, a film title that puns on their name or habit, and a birthday rating card.
An official-looking report about one real, harmless mishap everyone retells, with a typed log and a Replay button. Counters like 'Replays: 0, Lessons learned: 0' make the replay funnier each time.
best_for: Friends, siblings, close colleagues, close family

what_it_is: A short pixel-art animation, 6 scenes, of one real story or habit, using a small library of sprites (hair, outfit, bike, dog) recoloured to look like them. Chiptune bleeps carry the jokes.
lineage: New (Jordan.EXE style: inline SVG and CSS art, no image files)

what_it_is: A 4-panel comic: setup, escalation, twist, and a warm last panel. Speech bubbles use their real phrases. Drawn from a fixed character kit so it stays on-model.
A hushed narrator observes the recipient 'in the wild': habits become observed behaviours, their catchphrase is their 'signature call', and the herd of people who love them always returns.
A wall of 6 to 9 instant photos. Tap one to flip it and read the handwritten note on the back, written from a real memory. No photos? Sketch-style stand-ins keep the wall alive.

An uploaded photo transforms on screen (sketch, then colour) into stylized art: pixel, halftone pop, ASCII, comic ink, cross-stitch or sticker. The processing runs in the browser, so the photo never has to leave the device.
best_for: Family, friends, anyone with a good photo

what_it_is: A scrolling timeline of the person's story so far, one screen per milestone, ending on 'Now' and a wish for the next chapter. Each node is a small scene with a caption in the giver's voice.

A six-row performance review with star ratings and manager comments. Workplace-speak turns real traits into 'competencies', and the verdict promotes them to something warm. Works for the person or their pet.
The recipient taps their pet (or a beloved object) and it 'speaks' a random line in its own voice with a synthesized bark or meow. The tenth line is the warm one, unlocked after enough taps.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: companion scene, tap the dog (C-PET)

what_it_is: The recipient presses 'Run diagnostic' on the person (or their bike, car or espresso machine). Beeps rise, readings appear one row at a time, a control-group comparison lands, and the verdict ends on a compliment.

A collectible card for the recipient: rarity, funny-but-flattering stats, a special ability drawn from a real habit, and a flavour quote in their own words. It tilts and shines like a holographic card.
how_they_use_it: Tilt or drag to shine, tap to flip

what_it_is: A mock consulting briefing that 'explains' the person with a memorable framework: numbered parts, one-line insights from real habits, and animated charts with silly axes, ending on a warm recommendation.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: story briefing, the 'six Ds' parody (C-CHART)

what_it_is: A mock executive order that makes the birthday official: 'Whereas' clauses from real facts, numbered sections, a 'Sign into law' button with a stamp, a hidden memo that appears afterwards, and an absurd opposition response.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: birthday certificate, mock executive order (C-CERT)

what_it_is: A tap-through mock trial: the recipient is the defendant, charged with harmless 'crimes' from real habits. Exhibits, a witness (a person, a pet, or 'The Snacks'), a verdict and a warm silly sentence.
A vintage 'WANTED' poster for the recipient: an alias, affectionate 'crimes', where they were last seen and a reward the giver really offers. The portrait is a sepia photo treatment or a silhouette.

A scroll-to-accept terms and conditions for being their friend (or family member). Clauses satirize real habits, one clause is sincere, and the 'Decline' button dodges the cursor before the recipient gives in and accepts.
A dry product manual for the person, 'Model Jamie v40': what is in the box, getting started, care and feeding, a troubleshooting table of real habits, warnings, and a sincere lifetime warranty.

A professional-network-style profile with a silly headline, 'experience' from real places and hobbies, skills endorsed by their real friends, and two short 'recommendations' clearly marked as dramatizations.
An animated group chat where the friends 'plan' the birthday. Typing dots, a 'left on read' beat, a running joke, and a final reply from the recipient in their real catchphrase.
A split-flap airport or station board where every row is about the recipient: 'Jamie, DELAYED 10 min', 'Snacks, BOARDING', and the last row points to the cake. The board flutters into place.

Move a basket (or a character) to catch falling things for 30 seconds. Good items come from their obsessions, bad items are harmless jokes, and there is a golden bonus. Nobody loses: 'not yet' is a kind line.

A big button counts taps. Milestone messages fire at set counts, confetti at 10, and a warm secret waits far down the count. The 'stat' is something the recipient really does: espresso shots, laps, scoops.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: tap challenge and rep counter with milestones (C-REPS)

what_it_is: Each tap fills a gauge that stands for a real obsession (cups of coffee, laps, pages). The body reacts with escalating jitter, then the meter overflows into a celebration and a one-time 'decaf' gag resets it.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: fill meter, coffee to eight cups and the 'decaf' reset (C-FUEL)

what_it_is: A card-flip pairs game where every pair is a piece of their world (a trowel, a bike bell, the dog). Each match reveals a tiny fact or joke. Calm, no timer, no way to lose.

A marker slides back and forth and the recipient taps to stop it in the target zone, three rounds, each faster. The marker and target come from a real habit. Every result gets a funny line and the ending is warm whatever the score.

A prize wheel with 8 segments where every spin lands on something good: gifts the giver really offers, jokes from real facts, and warm messages. The third spin always lands on the hidden jackpot: the card's kindest line.
A small word puzzle built from the person's life: names, places, hobbies. Crossword clues are jokes and memories, and finding every word reveals a bonus message.

section: How Well Do You Know Them?
what_it_is: A 6-question multiple-choice quiz built only from real facts: one right answer, one plausible decoy, one absurd decoy. Funny reactions after each answer, and a results screen that lands warm at every score.

A fake 'Prove you're Jamie' verification: a 3x3 tile challenge ('Select all squares with snacks'), a checkbox that will not say 'I am not late', and a security question only they can answer. It ends with a 'Verified human' stamp.
The recipient types words (a noun, a food, a place) and the card writes a short story that stars them. The fixed text is real facts and the blanks make it absurd; the last line is warm and fixed.

A 'the year you arrived' page: what things cost, the number one songs, gadgets, headlines, then a closing 'And then you turned up'. Every item comes from a vetted data pack for that year, never from the model's memory.
Original lyrics set to a short synthesized track (chiptune, punk, lullaby, disco), with each line highlighted as it is sung. It sits on a cassette-style player with Side A, Side B and a bonus track.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: mixtape, Side A diss track and Side B punk 'Happy Birthday' (C-MUSIC)

what_it_is: A 16-pad sampler where each pad is a sound from their world ('Espresso hiss', 'Bike bell', their catchphrase). The recipient makes a beat, and a hidden pad combination unlocks a warm message.
Real voice messages from the giver and friends, shown as tapes or voicemails with a waveform. Hearing a real voice is often the biggest 'wow' in a card. The site writes the prompts, not the words.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: 'Side C', a real recorded voice message (C-MUSIC)

what_it_is: A soundboard of big buttons, one per real phrase they always say. Each plays the line (spoken or recorded) with a tiny animation. A hidden button turns their phrase into something kind.

A short handwritten-style letter that says the real reason the giver adores them. It calls back a joke from earlier in the card, tells one true story, states the truth in one plain line, and signs off. Usually the second-to-last section.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: taped closing note with two signatures (C-END)

what_it_is: A counter races up to the person's age while real reasons flick past. A handful stop and glow, the rest blur, and the last reason (the sincere one) lands on their exact age.

A booklet of 6 redeemable coupons the giver truly promises: 'One airport run, any hour', 'One bike tune-up'. A couple are jokes and one is a blank 'Ask me anything'. Redeeming shows a message the recipient can screenshot or send back.
best_for: Parents, partners, siblings, kids giving to parents

what_it_is: Every contributor gets a link to add a short message, a doodle or a photo. The card shows them as sticky notes on one wall. The site writes the invitation and the note starters.

The recipient taps to crack a cookie and reads a fortune. Five cookies: two funny predictions from real habits, two sincere lines, and a last one straight from the giver's heart, with lucky numbers that include their age.

A TV-style countdown of the 'Top 5 things about them', from number 5 to number 1, with a host intro and a drumroll before the last reveal. Number 1 is the sincere one. A 'skip to #1' link keeps it kind to impatient people.

A big red button starts a scripted launch (a software deploy, a rocket, a cake vault, a confetti cannon). Twelve typed status lines poke fun at their habits, then the payoff reveals the cake and sets off the ending.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: finale, big red 'Deploy birthday to production' button (C-FIN)

what_it_is: A cake with as many candles as their age (up to 9 shown, then '+31 more'). The recipient blows them out with the microphone or taps them out one by one, makes a wish, and the last candle triggers the final greeting and confetti.
how_they_use_it: Blow into the mic or tap
lineage: Jordan.EXE: finale, nine candles all out triggers the greeting (C-FIN)

what_it_is: Rolling end credits with fake job titles ('Snack Logistics: Brian'), a 'Special thanks' to the dog or the espresso machine, and a hidden tap target that reveals one last secret. It ends 'Refresh to replay'.
lineage: Jordan.EXE: credits line and 'refresh to reboot' ending (C-END)

what_it_is: Small badges pop up as the recipient explores: 'Bark Whisperer', 'Punctual? No.', 'Found the secret'. A list keeps score, and the last badge ('100%: Loved') unlocks once they have seen everything. It rewards curiosity and replays.
